cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has just finished a whole run of faithful work for the LORD. Then Sennacherib, king of Assyria, invades Judah and lays siege to its fortified cities, planning to take them for himself. Friend, that's like finally getting the whole kitchen spotless and somebody walks in wearing muddy boots.
Hezekiah sees that Sennacherib has come to make war against Jerusalem itself. Big king. Big army. BIG problem.

cards.question: When Hezekiah sees Sennacherib coming for Jerusalem, he makes his plan all by himself without talking to anyone.

cards.text: Hezekiah sits down with his leaders and mighty men. First thing on the table: the springs outside the city.

cards.question: Hezekiah and his leaders make a plan for the springs outside Jerusalem. What do they decide to do with them?

cards.text: And it's not just the leaders doing the work. Many people gather and stop up all the springs, plus the stream that flows through the land.

cards.question: Why do the people of Judah stop up all the springs and the stream?

answers.text: So Assyria won't find plenty of water
So Jerusalem's wells will stay full
So the enemy can't cross the stream

cards.text: Assyria's about to roll up thirsty and find out somebody shut the water off on PURPOSE. Meanwhile, Hezekiah works hard rebuilding every broken section of the wall and raising towers on it.

cards.question: Besides fixing the old wall, Hezekiah also builds an outer wall around the city.
Along with the walls and towers, what does Hezekiah produce an abundance of to get Jerusalem ready?

cards.text: Then Hezekiah puts military commanders over the people and gathers them in the square at the city gate for a pep talk. Friend, I once gave my oven a pep talk for twenty minutes and it STILL burned the whole batch.

cards.question: Hezekiah tells the people not to be afraid of the king of Assyria and his vast army. Why not?

answers.text: A greater One is with them
Assyria's army is smaller than it looks
Egypt is sending soldiers to help

cards.text: Then Hezekiah lays it out plain: "With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles."

cards.question: When Hezekiah says Sennacherib has only the arm of flesh on his side, what does he mean?
Hezekiah's speech leaves the people of Jerusalem shaken and discouraged.

cards.text: Later, while Sennacherib and all his forces besiege the city of Lachish, he sends his servants to Jerusalem with a message for Hezekiah and the people. Friend, nothing good has EVER come in a message that starts with "This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says".

cards.question: Sennacherib's message opens with a question for the people in Jerusalem. What does he ask them?

answers.text: What their confidence is based on
When they will open the gates

cards.text: He tells them Hezekiah is misleading them. He says they'll die by famine and thirst while Hezekiah keeps promising the LORD will deliver them.

cards.question: Sennacherib's message brings up something Hezekiah did in Judah's worship. What is it?

answers.text: Removing the high places and altars

cards.text: Then he brags about what he and his fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands. Have any of their gods been able to save their land from his hand?

cards.question: Sennacherib says no other nation's god could save it from him. So what's his point about the God of Judah?

answers.text: He is stronger than the rest

cards.text: He wraps up by telling them not to believe Hezekiah, because no god of any nation has saved its people from his hand. And his servants keep right on going, speaking even more against the LORD God and His servant Hezekiah.

cards.question: Sennacherib also writes letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.text: Speeches, then MORE speeches, then LETTERS, and this man is STILL not done. Now the Assyrians call out loudly, in Hebrew, to the people of Jerusalem standing on the wall.

cards.question: Why do the Assyrians shout in Hebrew to the people on Jerusalem's wall?

answers.text: To terrify them and capture the city
To offer them a peace deal
To call Hezekiah out to fight

cards.question: The Assyrians talk about the God of Jerusalem as if He were just like the gods of other peoples, made by human hands.

cards.text: Now meet the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. He and King Hezekiah answer all this noise together.

cards.question: With the Assyrians mocking the LORD, what do King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah do?

answers.text: Cry out to heaven in prayer
Lead the army out to fight

cards.question: Hezekiah and Isaiah cry out to heaven, and the LORD answers. What does He send into the camp of the king of Assyria?

cards.text: The angel wipes out every mighty man of valor and every leader and commander in Assyria's camp. And Sennacherib, the man with all the speeches and all the letters, goes back to his own land... in disgrace.

cards.question: Back home, Sennacherib walks into the temple of his god. What happens to him there?

answers.text: Some of his own sons strike him down
His priests crown him all over again
He falls sick and dies on the spot

cards.text: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and from all others, and He gave them rest on every side. After all that shouting, I bet the quiet sounded BEAUTIFUL.

cards.question: After all this, the nations look down on Hezekiah king of Judah.

cards.text: Many bring offerings to Jerusalem for the LORD, and valuable gifts for Hezekiah. And that's where we set the timer for now, friend, because Hezekiah's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The card says Hezekiah "keeps promising" the LORD will deliver them. Verse 11 only says "when he says" this. The word "keeps" adds a repeated action the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards hints at Hezekiah's changes to worship. Card 1 of stop 1 only says "a whole run of faithful work for the LORD." A baker can't reason out that Sennacherib brings up removing the high places and altars, so the pick comes down to luck. This stop already has several discovery questions (cards 2, 8, 14, 16), so this one shouldn't be one too.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The statement says the Assyrians talk about God "as if He were ... made by human hands." In verse 19, "the work of human hands" is the narrator describing the gods of the peoples. The verse says the Assyrians spoke against God as they had spoken against those gods. It doesn't say they called the LORD handmade. The card links the two things more tightly than the text does, and then asks the baker to mark that link True.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
